title: When the Clock Breaks
premise: In 1913 Liverpool, Ines Halloran drives for the Whitcombe family, whose matriarch is a celebrated suffragist — and whose household runs on secrets Ines reads in the mail she quietly opens. When a sealed letter reveals that patriarch Edmund Whitcombe has been laundering money through a shipping concern tied to a violent political faction, Ines realizes the family's escape plan aboard the morning steamer has only one berth left, and everyone will fight for it. As loyalties fracture and Edmund's corruption turns murderous, Ines must decide whether her found place among them is worth saving or worth exposing. In the end she gives the berth to the one person who never wanted it — Edmund's estranged daughter — and stays behind to testify, choosing truth over belonging.
about_author: Freya Thackeray is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing suffrage-era correspondence in northern England. She writes historical fiction about the people history filed under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Driver's Hands
chapters.summary: Ines Halloran's POV. We meet Ines as she chauffeurs Edith Whitcombe to a rally, establishing her habit of steaming open letters and her careful invisibility within the household. A small kindness from the youngest son, Tom, shows why she stays. Emotional beat: quiet longing disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Sealed in Wax
chapters.summary: Ines POV. A letter arrives bearing a seal she doesn't recognize; inside, an accusation against Edmund Whitcombe and a threat dated for the spring tide. Ines reseals it and delivers it, then can't sleep. Emotional beat: the reader's burden — knowledge as a weight she cannot put down.

chapters.title: What Edith Won't See
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Edith Whitcombe. Edith prepares for a triumphant speaking tour while Ines watches Edmund burn papers after midnight. Ines tests the waters with a carefully worded warning; Edith dismisses it. Emotional beat: the ache of loving someone who refuses to look.

chapters.title: The Daughter at the Gate
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Eleanor Whitcombe, estranged for eight years, returns unannounced — and Ines recognizes her name from the threatening letter. The two women circle each other, each suspecting the other. Emotional beat: wary recognition between two outsiders.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: Ines POV, with Tom. Ines and Tom find the shipping ledgers proving Edmund's money trail, but Tom wants to protect his father and Ines wants evidence. Their alliance strains. Emotional beat: the first crack in her found family.

chapters.title: One Berth
chapters.summary: Edmund POV. Edmund books passage for the family on the morning steamer — one berth only, he tells each member privately, letting them believe they've earned it. His charm curdles into menace. Emotional beat: power revealed as a game of scarcity he invented.

chapters.title: The Night of Broken Glass
chapters.summary: Ines POV. A break-in at the house; the threatening letter's sender demands the ledgers. Edmund lets Tom take the blame, and Tom is taken for questioning. Edith finally sees her husband clearly. Emotional beat: shattering of illusions, grief moving fast.

chapters.title: Bargains at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Eleanor POV. Eleanor offers Ines a deal: help her expose Edmund and share the berth. Ines, tempted, discovers Eleanor's own complicity in the scheme. Both women realize they are being played against each other. Emotional beat: two survivors learning trust is a risk worth taking.

chapters.title: The Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Climax. At the docks, Edmund confronts Ines with the opened letters, offering her the berth as payment for silence. She refuses, publicly hands the ledgers to a journalist, and names Eleanor for the berth instead. Edmund is arrested on the quay. Emotional beat: courage costing her everything she thought she wanted.

chapters.title: What Remains Unsealed
chapters.summary: Ines POV, weeks later. Testimony given, Tom cleared, Edith rebuilding her work without her husband's money. Eleanor writes from abroad; Ines answers honestly for the first time, no steam, no seal. Emotional beat: resolution — identity chosen over safety, family redefined rather than lost.
